function: Predicts the vehicle's next 2D position, hence the RSU transmit beamforming angle (proactive beamforming), from sub-6 GHz CSI, RGB images and depth maps (p. 3, 8).
system: RSU: 8/16/32-antenna mmWave ULA, 8-antenna sub-6 GHz array, RGB-D camera; vehicle: 8/16/32-antenna ULA; sub-6 GHz 80 MHz, 64 subcarriers; mmWave carrier not stated; no RIS (p. 3, 8).
method: MLP on CSI, ResNet-18 on RGB and depth, adaptive weight network, GRU (y) and MLP (x) regressors; supervised offline training, YOLOv5 pre-trained then fine-tuned (p. 4-8, 11).
data_channel: ViWi 'dist_cam' scenario; sub-6 GHz CSI generated from ViWi path parameters with reset path gains; random lane drifting added; separate random trajectories for training and testing (p. 8).
test_conditions: Same ViWi scenario, different random drifting trajectories for train and test; robustness test with dimmer images, CSI error -15 dB, depth noise variance 1 (p. 8, 13).
baselines: Non-learned: KF-T, EKF-T [18], DFRC-T [19]. Learned: DL-PB [22], V-A-BP [25], and own uni-modal I-PB, D-PB, C-PB (p. 10).
metrics: Angle prediction error (mean, standard deviation), achievable rate, outage probability, averaged over 300 realizations (p. 10-13).
openness: Code: https://github.com/Haotian-Zhang-PKU/Proactive-Beamforming-MMFF (p. 2); data built on the public ViWi framework, no dataset link.
q1_support: p. 8: "We simulate the sub-6 GHz CSI based on the wireless channel parameters provided by ViWi dataset"; ViWi is a public dataset, not a listed model, and the path gains are reset, so the reviewer should confirm.
q2_support: p. 8: "we randomly generate two entirely different trajectories" for training and testing, same scenario. The adverse-condition test (p. 13) adds noise to the test inputs, like a CSI-error sweep; no unseen scenario, site or array.
q3_support: p. 10: "A typical KF is adopted to track the vehicle" (non-learned KF-T, EKF-T, DFRC-T) and "an FC network is designed to estimate the current angular parameter" (learned DL-PB [22]); V-A-BP [25] is also learned; all compared on angle error, rate and outage (p. 11-13).
q4_support: p. 11: "Despite the increased complexity, MMFF-Net is first trained offline" is a qualitative remark; Table II (p. 9) lists layer widths only, with no FLOPs, parameter count or runtime.
q5_support: p. 2: "Simulation codes are provided to reproduce the results presented in this paper" with a GitHub link; training and testing also use the public ViWi framework (p. 8).
notes: Area 5 because the paper frames itself as ISAC with sensing-assisted communications (p. 2) and beamforming in an ISAC system is area 5; the beam serves communication only, so area 3 is the alternative. q1: ViWi is not a listed model, the paper never says ray tracing and it modifies the sub-6 GHz path gains (p. 8), so the reviewer should confirm. q2: Table V on p. 13 corrupts the test inputs of a model trained on clean data, which I treated as a noise test. Radar is simulated by noisy depth maps (p. 3, 6); the rate uses a LoS model (p. 9). The code URL spans a line break on p. 2.
